subject.title: [Feature]: Optional session activity watchdog and alerts (blocked by #39127)

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in session activity watchdog and operator alerting surface after the session activity API lands, or should core stop at activity/diagnostic signals for plugins and dashboards to consume?
rationale: The request adds new feature, config, delivery, privacy, UI/operator, and optional model-call behavior rather than fixing an existing contract, so automation cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Design core watchdog after activity API
options.body: Keep this issue open as the downstream product/design item once the canonical sessions.activity contract is settled.

options.title: Route alerting to plugins or dashboards
options.body: Expose core activity and diagnostics only, then let plugins, dashboards, or external operators own alert delivery and optional summaries.

options.title: Fold into broader stall recovery
options.body: Use this issue as context for broader stall visibility/recovery work, but require a narrower canonical implementation issue before coding.

recommendation.title: Design core watchdog after activity API
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the downstream product/design item once the canonical sessions.activity contract is settled.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the strongest live signal for the upstream session activity contract this watchdog depends on.
